# onpager_integration (Resource)

Manage an OnPager source integration, including optional Alertmanager polling.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "onpager_integration" "example" {
  name        = "Metrics"
  source_kind = "alertmanager"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Nonempty integration name without leading or trailing whitespace.
- `source_kind` (String) Source format: `alertmanager`, `grafana_unified`, `grafana_legacy`, or `generic_onpager_v1`. Changing it replaces the integration.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the integration accepts events and permits configured polling. Defaults to `true`. Disabled integrations remain in state.
- `polling` (Attributes) Polling settings, accepted only for `alertmanager`. Omission or `null` disables polling while the server retains disabled settings. Enabling polling lets the backend contact `base_url`; the provider sends no immediate poll command. Secrets are stored in Terraform state and cannot be recovered on import. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--polling))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Stable nonzero canonical lowercase OnPager UUID.
- `revision` (Number) Integration settings revision used in strong numeric `If-Match` for updates and deletion. Stale revisions report a conflict; run a new plan before retrying.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) One-time webhook credential returned on creation. Preserved across refresh and updates; unavailable after import. Stored in Terraform state even though normal display is hidden by the sensitive marking. Token rotation is not implemented.
- `webhook_path` (String) Ingress webhook path supplied by the server for this integration.
- `webhook_url` (String) Ingress webhook URL supplied when the server configures its public base URL; otherwise `null`. Never derived from the Control endpoint.

<a id="nestedatt--polling"></a>
### Nested Schema for `polling`

Required:

- `base_url` (String) Explicit nonempty HTTP(S) base URL, required even when polling is disabled. Must have a host and no user information, query, fragment, encoded path, backslashes, or dot path segments. Trailing slashes are accepted.

Optional:

- `auth_kind` (String) Authentication kind: `none` (default), `basic`, or `bearer`. `none` forbids credentials; `basic` uses username/password; `bearer` uses only token.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the backend polls the configured endpoint. Defaults to `false`. Polling also requires the integration to be enabled.
- `interval_seconds` (Number) Polling interval in whole seconds, from 15 through 3600. Defaults to 60; zero is invalid.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Basic authentication password, only for `basic`. Omission or `null` preserves a saved server secret; an empty string explicitly replaces it with an empty password. Configured values persist in Terraform state even though marked sensitive; the API never returns the secret.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) Bearer polling credential, only for `bearer`. Omission or `null` preserves a saved server secret. A replacement must be nonempty and contain no whitespace or control characters. Configured values persist in Terraform state even though marked sensitive; the API never returns the secret.
- `username` (String) Basic authentication username. Defaults to an empty string; a nonblank username is required for `basic`. Must be empty for `none` or `bearer`.

Read-Only:

- `has_secret` (Boolean) Whether the backend stores a polling credential. This flag does not reveal or recover the secret.

## Import

Import using the integration UUID. Import cannot recover the one-time webhook
token or saved polling credentials.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_integration.example
  id = "aaaaaaaa-aaaa-4aaa-8aaa-aaaaaaaaaaaa"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_integration.example aaaaaaaa-aaaa-4aaa-8aaa-aaaaaaaaaaaa
```

## Lifecycle

The API supplies the Ingress webhook path and any public URL; the provider does
not derive Ingress from the Control endpoint. Only Alertmanager integrations
support polling. Enabling polling schedules backend requests to the configured
endpoint; Terraform operations do not execute polls or rotate tokens.

Removing `polling` disables polling while the API retains its settings. An
omitted block remains null while polling is disabled. Import adopts enabled
polling settings; disabled settings are adopted only when configured in HCL.

Updates and destroy use the integration's observed numeric revision. Conflicts
report a diagnostic without retrying. Creating with `enabled = false` saves the
allocated identity and token before disabling; polling settings are saved with
that disabled update. Committed writes are saved before later reads, preserving
ownership and received secrets if a later operation fails.

Destroy hides the integration and revokes webhook and polling credentials,
preserving alerts, historical references and accepted work. Restoration is
unsupported. Only confirmed absence removes state during refresh.

## Secrets

The webhook token is returned once on create and retained across refresh and
updates. Import cannot recover it. Null polling secrets preserve saved
credentials; an explicit empty Basic password replaces it with an empty value.

Webhook tokens, polling credentials and configuration persist in Terraform
state. Sensitive attributes hide normal display but do not encrypt state files.
Authenticated polling requires the backend credential keyring to be configured.

## Permissions

Requires tenant grants `integrations.create`, `integrations.read`,
`integrations.update`, `integrations.disable` when disabling, and
`integrations.delete` for destroy.
